summary: A first-person narrator says goodbye to Steve, who is leaving for a couple of days, and resolves to search for Sarah, who was taken by Ramos to the Peten, with Alan's reluctant help. Alan admits unease about the people who rule the place and agrees to take the narrator to look once the weather clears. The narrator then settles into a budget hotel room and decides to call St. Vincent's to check on Lou and tell him what is happening. The excerpt is part 115 of Book 3 of a fiction work.
one_line: The narrator sends Steve away, plans a dangerous search for Sarah in the Peten with Alan, and calls St. Vincent's to check on Lou.
key_facts: Steve tells the narrator that it is only for a couple of days and that they will both be okay if they stick together.
The narrator watches Steve's Jeep blend into the smoggy haze of the avenue after he leaves.
The narrator resolves to find Sarah before something else truly horrible happens to her.
The narrator intends to keep Steve as safely distant from the search as possible.
The narrator recalls going down into the four-hundred-year-old subterranean harem quarters of the Red Fort in Agra.
In the Red Fort harem quarters the narrator was surrounded by screaming bats and knee-deep in guano, with only a flashlight.
Alan says he will plead guilty to a deep-seated disquiet about the people who rule the placid paradise.
Alan agrees to take the narrator up for a quick look, but only after the weather clears.
The narrator says the Peten is where Sarah ended up the first time and is where Ramos has likely taken her now.
The narrator names Baalum as the place Alan says, and believes he means every word.
The hotel room has off-brand carpet the color of decaying vegetation and two double beds, one used only as a suitcase shelf.
The narrator plans to call St. Vincent's to check on Lou and tell him what is happening.
The narrator does not want a lecture from Lou about the recklessness of the plan and says they need support, not male advice.
The narrator asks the desk for the local AT&T contact number before making the call.
